During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Canadian police suspend use of Crime Stoppers after 1.5 million records exposed
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Canadian police services are suspending their use of Crime Stoppers after a breach exposed more than 1.5 million tips submitted across Canada over 25 years, a CBC News investigation found. More than 850,000 records included personally identifiable information. The tips were managed through P3, software provided by U.S.-based Navigate360. Navigate360 acknowledged on Friday that its database had been breached between November 2025 and March 2026 and said potentially exposed information included names, addresses, birth dates and Social Security numbers. The company said it had no evidence the information had been used for fraud or identity theft. Police in several provinces have paused their use of the service while they assess the breach and its safeguards. Toronto and Ottawa police are directing people to report information through police channels, which do not necessarily offer the same anonymity. Crime Stoppers chapters and police are seeking further details from Navigate360. The company said it hired a cybersecurity firm to help strengthen security.

items.title: [farmer.pl] Farmers urged to shred corn stalks to curb pests and disease
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

As Poland’s corn harvest continues, agronomic guidance recommends finely shredding stalks and other crop residues after harvest to reduce winter shelter for the European corn borer and limit disease in the next season. The borer’s larvae overwinter in stalks, while feeding damage can promote Fusarium infections that contaminate grain with mycotoxins. Residue management also affects soil organic matter: grain corn leaves substantial biomass in the field, while silage harvesting removes nearly all above-ground material. Guidance recommends accounting for soil moisture and the next crop; working wet soil can cause compaction, and fields vulnerable to erosion may need residue left on the surface.

items.title: [zmescience.com] Protein evidence identifies Chinese fossils as Denisovans, revealing likely facial traits
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Researchers have identified human fossils from Xujiayao in northern China as Denisovans using ancient proteins, then compared their bones with other remains to infer the group’s likely appearance. The fossils suggest Denisovans had low, backward-sloping foreheads, heavy brow ridges and broad, relatively flat faces, with features distinct from those of Neanderthals. The team recovered a Denisovan-linked collagen variant from two fossils with no surviving DNA. The Xujiayao collection includes 20 specimens excavated decades ago. items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

A wildfire that killed four soldiers and injured 39 at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright began during routine training on an automatic grenade launcher range, Canadian military police said Thursday. The fire began inside a restricted danger area where firefighters could not attack it directly. A shift in wind direction and speed then drove the flames into another training area where soldiers were practising. As of Thursday, 27 injured members remained in hospital, including 13 in critical condition. Investigators have established the fire’s origin but are examining why it was not initially considered a threat and why live-fire training took place in the afternoon during a high-risk fire month. Wainwright’s range guidance recommends early-morning firing between August and October, and officials said they would review the decision to proceed. Military police, a military Board of Inquiry and Alberta’s Chief Medical Examiner are conducting separate investigations. The inquiry will examine training and safety procedures. Chief of the Defence Staff Gen. Jennie Carignan said interim safety changes would be made quickly if needed. The board’s findings will be made public when complete.

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to pause fighting around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations under an arrangement brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, officials said Friday. The White House had announced Oct. 29 as the ceasefire’s start date, while Ukrainian negotiator Dmytro Lubinets, the country’s human rights ombudsman, said the humanitarian mission would begin on Oct. 29 and the pause would last several days. Oleshky’s population has fallen from about 24,000 before the invasion to an estimated 1,700-2,000, including about 50 children. Residents face shortages of food, medicine and clean water, limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks. The first steps are expected to include assessing residents’ needs and clearing mines before aid convoys enter. Civilian teams are to coordinate transport for those choosing to leave for either Russia or Ukraine. The ceasefire is expected to cover the Kherson region and neighboring areas essential to the operation. Lubinets said it would last several days; officials have not provided details on how compliance will be monitored. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said technical-level talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: [npr.org] AI-discovered PHP flaws prompt website shutdowns as exploit attempts surge
items.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

Researchers using artificial intelligence uncovered two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by about 70% of websites. Security updates were released on Oct. 21. The flaws could let attackers run malicious code on affected servers without logging in, potentially stealing data or disrupting websites. Organizations rushed to patch systems, while some government and private websites were temporarily taken offline as a precaution. Cloudflare chief executive Matthew Prince said attempts to exploit the flaws rose from thousands before public disclosure to tens of thousands within 45 minutes, hundreds of thousands within two hours and millions afterward. The PHP Foundation said Chainguard broke an embargo before the fix was ready, while Chainguard CEO Dan Lorenc said he believed the flaw was already being exploited. Security agencies urged operators to install patches, and researchers cautioned that attempts to exploit a flaw do not necessarily mean attackers have working tools.

items._excerpt: Researchers using artificial intelligence uncovered two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by about 70% of websites. The flaws could let attackers run malicious code on affected servers without logging in, potentially stealing data or disrupting websites (nation.com.pk, npr.org). Organizations rushed to patch systems, while some government and private websites were temporarily taken offline as a precaution (theguardian.com, npr.org). Cloudflare chief executive Matthew Prince said attempts to exploit the flaws rose from thousands before public disclosure to tens of thousands within 45 minutes, hundreds of thousands within two hours and millions afterward (theguardian.com, politico.eu). The PHP Foundation said Chainguard broke an embargo before the fix was ready, while Chainguard CEO Dan Lorenc said he believed the flaw was already being exploited (politico.eu). Security agencies urged operators to install patches, and researchers cautioned that attempts to exploit a flaw do not necessarily mean attackers have working tools (npr.org, reuters.com). Other security issues: The same week brought a Node.js flaw, vulnerabilities in Plex, breaches involving AI gateway LiteLLM and development platform Railway, and concerns over a weak cryptographic key used by Indian certificate authority eMudhra (reuters.com). Human verification: Wiz researcher Sagi Tzadik said the AI agent could not explain how it had found the PHP bug; his team spent days tracing its cause and reproducing it (time.com). Discovery rate: Research by threat-intelligence firm VulnCheck found that AI helped drive a year-over-year doubling in discovered digital flaws. Experts say exploit development that once took weeks or months can now take hours (reuters.com). Limits of user control: Experts said visitors cannot patch a service provider’s website themselves; operators must deploy fixes and limit the damage compromised

Between the cork oaks and the Vicentina Coast, Herdade da Matinha was born from an abandoned Alentejo estate, whose chimney still bears the date 1917. This rural tourism project, developed by SABRAB Architecture in collaboration with the owner Alfredo Moreira da Silva, starts from a simple principle: to make use of what already existed and add only what was necessary, with the same economy of means that has always characterized rural construction in the Alentejo region.
